title: Bracketed Blue-Green Orchestration Notebook
content:
Context / intent:
Quick personal notebook to capture a blue-green style flip that uses bracketed traffic windows and anchor cohorts rather than a single canary bucket. Meant for medium-risk model flips (non-breaking API changes, model variant updates that can affect hallucination or latency).

Top-level idea (short):
- Maintain two parallel fleets (blue/green) with identical configs except model version.
- Use small, anchored cohorts (10–50 tenants) to hold traffic steady across the flip.
- Bracketed ramp windows: short bursts of higher traffic followed by hold windows to observe regression (think: spike -> hold -> expand).

Why bracketed vs continuous ramp?
- Forces quick stress on the new variant to expose tail-latency and failure modes.
- Hold windows provide time for manual signal checks and automated evaulation.

Preflight checklist (things I must verify before starting):
- [ ] Infra: green fleet healthy, all node pools at desired capacity (kubectl get pods -n inference Green-*)
- [ ] Telemetry probes: synthetic set (fast/slow/hallucination prompts) running against both fleets and logging into /rollouts/synthetics
- [ ] Feature flags: ensure per-tenant pin toggle exists and can be applied via admin-api (test on dev-tenant 999)
- [ ] Circuit breakers: global and per-tenant rate limits, backpressure thresholds set (ruleset: rb-2025-11)
- [ ] Rollback job: verified that unpin + routing revert returns to baseline in < 3 minutes during dry-run
- [ ] Notifiers: #release-alerts + oncall pager rotation set for the entire night-window

Bracketing schedule (example):
- Window 0 (T0): anchor cohort A (20 tenants) moved to green (5% of global traffic) for 12m (warmup 5m, hold 7m)
- Window 1 (T0+12m): expand to 15% by adding anchor cohort B (additional 30 tenants) for 12m (5m ramp, 7m hold)
- Window 2 (T0+24m): spike to 35% for 6m to test burst behavior (2m ramp, 4m hold)
- Window 3 (T0+30m): hold at 35% for 30m if signals clean, else immediate pinback/rollback
- Final: full flip overnight only if SLA/quality metrics remain within thresholds for 2 consecutive holds

Anchor cohort rules (notes):
- Choose tenants with low churn, predictable traffic patterns, and good telemetry coverage (we can diagnose). Avoid high-risk enterprise customers without explicit opt-in.
- Maintain a small set of canary tenants that are always used across flips (consistency improves signal comparability).
- For each tenant, ensure client SDK version compatibility; note any pinned fallback behavior.

Signals to monitor (automated + manual):
- Latency P95/P99 per-route and per-tenant (thresholds: P95 +15%, P99 +30% relative to baseline)
- Error rate spikes (5xx or model-level errors) > 0.5% absolute increase triggers alert
- Quality regressions: synthetic eval error score delta > 3% or hallucination rate increase > 2pp
- Token cost delta (unit economics): > +20% vs baseline is a red flag
- End-user UX regressions: negative feedback survey rate > 1.5% in anchor cohorts

Quick rollback decision rules (cheats):
- SEV: any cascading 5xx leading to autoscale thrashing -> immediate rollback
- Latency: P99 > 2x baseline for > 2 consecutive hold windows -> rollback
- Quality: synthetic eval delta violates threshold AND nontrivial user escalations -> rollback
- Cost: sustained > 20% unit cost without commensurate quality improvements -> rollback to cheaper quantized variant

Operational commands (personal clipboard):
- Pin tenant to blue (fast): curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://admin.redwood/api/v1/tenants/123/pin -d '{"target":"blue"}'
- Unpin (release to routing): curl -X POST https://admin.redwood/api/v1/tenants/123/unpin
- Route split (traffic): admin-cli route split set --from blue --to green --percent 15 --policy bracketed-2025
- Emergency full revert: admin-cli rollout revert --target blue --force --comment "immediate-rollback");

Warmup behavior notes:
- Warmup entails two phases: (1) low-volume prefix tests to populate KV/cache; (2) synthetic user-like load to prime attention caches.
- Warmup should not exceed 6–8 minutes for the majority of tenants; longer for large-context workflows.

Per-tenant pinning tactics (edge cases):
- For tenants with multiple clients, pin at tenant-level only if majority of calls use the same route; otherwise coordinate client-side SDK toggles.
- For enterprise tenants requiring manual sign-off, use a soft-pin (80/20 green/blue with manual rollback allowed) until legal/ops ok.

Post-flip validation and latency budget reconciliation:
- After final flip, run a 3-hour hold with expanded synthetic suite and business KPI checks (conversions, retention proxies).
- Update cost/latency dashboard with model version tag (version metadata: model_x_v3.2) and save snapshot.

Open questions / TODOs to resolve before next flip:
- What is the canonical small synthetic set that surfaces hallucination regressions reliably? (ask ML-evals team)
- Can we automate bracket window progression based on signal thresholds (instead of manual ping)?
- Need a pre-authenticated rollback script that non-sre leads can run safely (add safeties: dry-run, confirm tenant count).
- Validate that our caching warmup actually populates same KV keys as production traffic for long-context tenants (esp. doc-summarization flows).

Notes-to-self (brief):
- Keep anchor cohorts constant across successive flips for signal hygiene.
- Prefer bracketed spikes over slow ramp for catching tail issues.
- When in doubt, prefer pin back: fast, observable, and low blast radius.

References / quick links:
- Linear ticket for this flip: REDW-1023 (planning)
- Rollout helper scripts: github.com/redwood-inference/release-scripts (look at bluegreen.sh)
- Prior flip notes: internal release notebook from 2025-06 (search: "flip-log 2025-06")
